name: Liver and Heart Footprint — Phase 1 core engine
goal: A Python package (src/lhf) that turns a real Indian recipe (ingredient lines as written on the web) into per-serving nutrient totals and daily-budget bars, where every number traces to a cited source row. Spec: docs/SPEC.md.
rules: Python: /home/prtyksh/subjects/cgas_env/bin/python (3.12). Allowed third-party libraries: pandas, numpy, openpyxl. Nothing else; no pip install.
Run code as PYTHONPATH=src ... ; the package is src/lhf.

No numbers invented in code: src/lhf/*.py may only contain the numeric literals 0-12, 100, 1000. Every other number is read from data/curated/*.csv (acceptance/test_rules.py checks this at every done).

Never modify data/raw, data/samples, docs/SPEC.md, acceptance/, or the architect's data/curated tables (measures.csv, constants.csv, classes.csv, baselines.csv). If one looks wrong, write a note and stop; do not work around it.
No network access in code (no requests/urllib/http/socket), no randomness, no subprocess in src/.
Never copy test inputs or expected answers into code or data. Gold lines must not appear in src/ or aliases.csv; a hidden test set is run later by the user.
If a line, ingredient or quantity cannot be handled, return the documented UNQUANTIFIED/UNMAPPED/UNQUANTIFIABLE result. Never default to a guessed number (e.g. 100 g).
Read AGENTS.md (project rules) once at the start of the session.

forbidden.message: no browser automation or anti-bot bypass tools
code must not read the gold/test answers

tasks.title: Constants and unified food composition table
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §2. Build lhf.paths, lhf.constants.get and lhf.composition (load_table, get, nutrients_for) combining the IFCT 2017 transcription (542 rows), INDB UK (144) and INDB US (54) into one table with the exact columns, units, missing-value rules and the oils energy fix described in §2. Useful reading (do not import it): experiments/ifct_check/replicate.py shows how the raw files are read; data/raw/ifct2017_transcription/PROVENANCE.md explains the oils defect.

tasks.title: Nutrient summing (validated against INDB's 1,014 published dishes)
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §3. Implement lhf.compute.NUTRIENTS and sum_nutrients(items). The acceptance test converts INDB's own recipes to grams with INDB's rules and checks your sums reproduce INDB's published per-100 g values (>= 99.5% of dishes for energy, fat, SFA, sodium, protein, fibre, free sugar; >= 95% for carbohydrate). If agreement is low, the bug is in summing or in T1's table, not in the test.

tasks.title: Ingredient line parser
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §4. Implement lhf.parse.parse_line(text) returning exactly the keys in §4. Real lines are in data/samples/recipes_phase1.jsonl (1,339 lines from 71 recipes, incl. Hindi lines, unicode fractions, ranges, '2-1/2' mixed numbers, HTML entities, stated grams in brackets). The test scores per-field accuracy on 120 hand-labelled lines (acceptance/gold/gold_public.json) and checks invariants on all 1,339 lines. Write general rules; do not special-case gold lines (a hidden set of 40 more lines is run later).

tasks.title: Ingredient name matcher and alias table
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §5. Create data/curated/aliases.csv (alias,code,note) with general Indian/Hindi/English ingredient names (look at the parsed names of all sample lines to see what is needed, and look up codes in the composition table with composition.load_table()). Implement lhf.match.match_name(name). Codes must exist in the composition table; prefer IFCT codes, but INDB_UK T5xx codes for fats/oils. Aliases are short names, never whole lines. Fuzzy cutoff comes from constants (FUZZY_MATCH_CUTOFF).

tasks.title: Household measures to grams
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §6 and data/curated/measures_README.md. Implement lhf.grams.grams_for(qty, unit, size, stated_g, stated_ml, code) applying rules 1-9 in order, reading data/curated/measures.csv and constants (PINCH_FRACTION_OF_TSP). Return basis and flags exactly as named in §6. Never return a default when no rule applies: return None with basis UNQUANTIFIABLE.

tasks.title: Food classes: added sugar, refined carbohydrate, salt, fat sources
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §7. Implement lhf.classify.classes_for(code) and class_totals(items) from data/curated/classes.csv. A code can have several classes (e.g. salt is SALT and SPICE).

tasks.title: Daily-budget footprint
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §8. Implement lhf.footprint.footprint(per_serving, setting, risk) reading every limit and reference value from data/curated/baselines.csv and constants.csv, listing the ids used in limit_sources.

tasks.title: End-to-end recipe pipeline and command line
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §9. Implement lhf.pipeline.analyse_recipe(recipe, setting, risk) wiring parse -> match -> grams -> composition -> classify -> footprint, with the exact output structure, exclusion reasons and warnings of §9, and lhf.cli. Output must be JSON-serialisable with no NaN. Totals must equal the sum of included lines. Test it on data/samples/recipes_phase1.jsonl.

tasks.title: Validation run against lab-analysed dishes (report generated from results)
tasks.spec: Read docs/SPEC.md sections 0-1 and the section named below completely before writing code. Inspect the real input files (head/describe them) instead of assuming their format. Section: §10. Write experiments/phase1_validation/run.py that writes results.json and then REPORT.md generated from results.json by code (never type numbers by hand). Required REPORT.md sections: Summary, Per-dish table, By setting, Coverage, Limitations. There is no target ratio: report what comes out, plainly; never use the words 'proves' or 'conclusively'.
